facts.note: Female "femme fatale" Photuris fireflies mimic the photic signaling patterns of the smaller Photinus, attracting males to what appears to be a suitable mate, then eating them. This provides the females with a supply of the toxic defensive lucibufagin chemicals.

They engage in aggressive mimicry, imitating the light signals that other firefly species' females use to attract mates – but Photuris use it to attract, kill and eat the unsuspecting males of those other species. / (Firefly 문서 참고문헌) "...its effects on the evolution of flash signaling in other New World fireflies".
Fireflies produce a "cold light", with no infrared or ultraviolet frequencies.
